questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to consider the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

**Statements:**

Some devices are electronics.

All electronics are mobiles.

No mobile is a phone.

**Conclusions:**

(I) : No phone is a device.

(II) : At least some electronics are phones.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73a642ee34bdadd3c2c8b0066fc9158d06127b336d76c140038f8f0e384c18af.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) No phone is a device → Does not follow (As some devices are electronics, all electronics are mobiles and no mobile is a phone. So it is possible but not definite)

(II) At least some electronics are phones → Does not follow (As all electronics are mobiles and no mobile is a phone. As whole electronics comes in mobiles which cannot be phone, therefore it is false)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow from the statements.

**Statements:**

All cushions are quilts.

All pillows are quilts.

All quilts are beds.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cushions are beds.

II. Some pillows are beds.

III. Some cushions are pillows.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f3fabb45b83c9a82090be069581d80251a2b2790168a77818696386dfcd94f3e.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some cushions are beds → Follow (As all cushions are quilts and all quilts are beds. As whole cushions comes in quilts which whole comes in beds, therefore it is true.)

II. Some pillows are beds → Follow (As all pillows are quilts and all quilts are beds. As whole pillows comes in quilts which whole comes in beds, therefore it is true.)

III. Some cushions are pillows → Does not follow (As all cushions are quilts and all pillows are quilts. So it is possible but not definite)

∴ Here, Only conclusions I and II follow.​

questions.question: 42 is related to 36 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 57 is related to 144. Which of the following numbers is related to 81 related using the same logic?

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.

questions.question: K, L, M, W, X, Y and Z scored different marks in an exam. K scored more than only three people. Y scored less than only L and M. W scored more than Z but less than X. L did not score the highest marks. How many people scored less than X?

M > L > Y > K > X > W > Z

Thus, according to the final arrangement two people scored less than X.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Ramesh wants to visit his childhood friend’s house. Ramesh’s friend explained his house directions over a text message. See the below text sent to Ramesh about the direction of his friend’s house and answer the following question accordingly. “When you step out of your house, you are facing north. Take a right and walk 3 km, you will see a T-point/junction. Take a right and walk 2 km. There will be a roundabout with four roads. Take the second left from the roundabout and walk 1 km. Take a right and walk 3 km. Take a right and walk 1 km. You will find my house at the front.” In which direction is Ramesh facing when he takes the second left from the roundabout?
questions.solution:
Given: Ramesh wants to visit his childhood friend’s house. Ramesh’s friend explained his house directions over a text message.

When you step out of your house, you are facing north.

Take a right and walk 3 km, you will see a T-point/junction.

Take a right and walk 2 km. There will be a roundabout with four roads. 

Take the second left from the roundabout and walk 1 km. 

Take a right and walk 3 km. 

Take a right and walk 1 km. You will find my house at the front.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ccd8ef9fc1f2fec7b9645a925e17b711243cd99f376b0cfbcb1afb7798d5c5ce.png] 

Thus, Ramesh is facing in the south direction when he takes the second left from the roundabout.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Here, specifically "Roundabout" is mentioned, so accordingly counting clockwise from the roundabout - 2nd left will be in the south direction.

Furthermore, it is also mentioned "There will be a roundabout with four roads.", so 4 roads are of the four direction, therefore at the roundabout when counted clockwise:

Ramesh (Facing south) → 1st road

1st left (east) → 2nd road

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All dogs are sheep.

All wolves are foxes.

All sheep are wolves.

**Conclusions:**

I. All wolves are sheep.

II. All dogs are foxes.

III. All dogs are wolves.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.
Only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4f45d3da61aded431a8087975ce95e607f00a6b48707464601615f386b26b8a.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All wolves are sheep → Does not follow (As all sheep are wolves. So it is possible but not definite)

II. All dogs are foxes → Follow (As all dogs are sheep, all sheep are wolves and all wolves are foxes. As whole dogs comes in sheep which whole comes in wolves which whole comes in foxes, therefore it is true.)

III. All dogs are wolves → Follow (As all dogs are sheep and all sheep are wolves. As whole dogs comes in sheep which whole comes in wolves, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusions II and III follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
